title: Landing angles: speed, cost, trust experiments
content:
Objective:
Quick experiments to find a homepage hero that converts core developer users (fast prototypes) and platform leads (cost predictability + SLAs). Draft copy spans three principal trade-off angles: performance (latency/throughput), unit economics (cost/per-token and autoscaling), and operational trust (security, SLAs, private deploys).

Context / audience:
- Primary: Software and ML engineers evaluating hosted inference for production integrations.
- Secondary: Platform/infra leads shopping for Dedicated/Private contracts with SLAs and predictable capacity.
- Tertiary: Executive decision makers focused on vendor risk, cost, and compliance.

Top-line positioning hypothesis:
"Redwood Inference gives you predictable, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — so teams spend less time babysitting models and more time shipping features."
(Working — we want shorter hero variants below.)

Hero variants (short + punchy):
A. "Production LLMs that behave: fast, cheap, and reliable."
   Subhead: "Same API. Multiple deployment profiles. Predictable latency, unit costs, and SLAs for every stage of scale."

B. "Ship LLM features with confidence — latency and costs you can measure."
   Subhead: "Hosted for fast launch. Dedicated for throughput. Private for compliance. One runtime, one API."

C. "From prototype to mission-critical: inference that scales and saves."
   Subhead: "Autoscaling pools, smart batching, and routing policies that cut per-token spend without sacrificing SLOs."

D. "Unify your LLM stack: performance controls, cost insights, and enterprise-grade privacy."
   Subhead: "Traceable requests, rollout controls, and predictable pricing — with optional VPC/on-prem."

Hero tone / microcopy notes:
- Variant A is blunt and aimed at engineering leaders who care about operational metrics. Use short, declarative sentences.
- Variant B emphasizes the API continuity and simplicity for fast adoption. Good for top-of-funnel developer landing.
- Variant C appeals to product managers/engineers who span prototyping->production. Includes economic framing (saves).
- Variant D targets procurement/security audiences; use words like "traceable", "privacy", "VPC", "SLA".

Primary CTA ideas (prioritized):
- "Start free — 5k tokens" (developer funnel)
- "Request dedicated pricing" (enterprise funnel)
- Secondary CTA: "See latency & cost benchmarks" (link to benchmark docs)

Product page copy snippets (short blocks we can reuse) :
- Hosted API: "Start in minutes with a developer-friendly REST/SDK. Streaming, function calling, and a curated model catalog with verified performance profiles."
- Dedicated: "Reserved GPU pools and SLA-backed throughput. Configure autoscaling, burst capacity, and private capacity draws for predictable performance."
- Private: "Deploy behind your VPC or on-prem. Customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs for regulated workloads."
- Console (Observability): "Per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and rollout controls for safe releases and fast troubleshooting."
- Optimize: "Policy-driven batching, quantization suggestions, and quality-monitoring tied to prompt sets to reduce unit costs without losing signal."

Competitive angle + differentiation bullets (short):
- Versus general cloud AI endpoints: "Redwood is inference-first — we optimize latency and unit economics at the request plane, not just expose model servers."
- Versus LLM API incumbents: "We offer deployment flexibility (Dedicated, Private) and traceable controls for enterprise use cases where simple APIs aren’t enough."
- Versus self-hosted inference runtimes: "You get a unified control plane plus operational tooling (rollouts, canaries, cost dashboards) without building orchestration layers yourself."

Key claims we must be able to substantiate (engineering + docs owners):
- "Predictable tail latency under p95 for common generator models" (need benchmark pages & methodology)
- "X% per-token cost reduction with intelligent batching & caching on typical query mixes" (need workload study)
- "SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated customers" (contract language)
- "Private deployments with KMS and audit logs" (security docs)

Competitor callouts to test on page (honest, not named slams):
- 'Vendor A' — simple API but limited deployment options and poor cost controls at scale.
- 'Vendor B' — good performance but SaaS-only; handshake issues for regulated workloads.
- 'Open runtime setups' — flexible but high ops cost and missing rollout/traceability.
(Engineering/Legal: ensure we avoid trademarked names in final public copy.)

Homepage modules (order suggestion + short copy):
1) Hero (choose 1 of A–D)
2) Trust bar: logos + short stats: "Used by 200+ teams" "99.95% uptime (Dedicated)" "Avg. dev time to prod: 2 days" (need to validate numbers)
3) How it works (3 columns): Runtime optimizations, Smart routing, Deployment abstraction (one-liners)
4) Product flavors (cards for Hosted, Dedicated, Private) with CTAs
5) Benchmarks snapshot: latency/cost charts (link to deep dive)
6) Customer stories / short quotes: target 2 dev-focused + 1 security/compliance quote
7) Footer CTAs: start free / contact sales

A/B test plan (quick):
- Test 1: Hero variant A vs B (developer-centric vs API continuity) — metric: sign-ups (new API keys), time window 2 weeks, target traffic: product blog referral + docs.
- Test 2: Primary CTA text "Start free" vs "Get dedicated pricing" based on visitor segments (detect company email domain) — metric: CTA clicks -> form completions.
- Test 3: Benchmarks snapshot on homepage vs buried in product page — metric: bounce rate and benchmark click-throughs, conversion for mid-market leads.

Measurement and instrumentation notes:
- Funnel events: hero_cta_click, api_key_created, pricing_inquiry_started, benchmark_click, dedicated_form_submit.
- Tag pages with experiment ids and wire to amplitude/GA4 and internal product analytics.

Open questions / decisions for next review:
- Which hero variant should be default for paid channels? (Recommend variant B for developer-focused campaigns, variant D for enterprise ABM landing pages.)
- Do we have validated numbers for 'avg dev time to prod' and 'teams using Redwood'? (Product analytics to confirm.)
- Are we comfortable referencing specific latency percentiles on the marketing site or should we keep language vague and link to detailed benchmarks?

Next steps / owners:
- Product marketing: pick 2 hero variants and 2 CTA combos for launch (Owner: Priya Singh) — due 2025-02-23
- Engineering: publish benchmark methodology + dataset for public benchmark page (Owner: Ethan Chen) — due 2025-03-07
- Design: hero art direction and micro-illustrations for module 3 (Owner: Marco Ruiz) — due 2025-02-27

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally copy-first — not final UX. Want quick iteration on messaging resonance.
- Keep legal/engineering looped for any specific numeric claims.
- If you have short customer quotes we can use as authenticity signals, paste below or link the support ticket id.

Scratch ideas (one-liners to consider):
- "Inference that scales like code — predictable, inspectable, versioned."
- "Turn unpredictable LLM costs into a KPI you can own."
- "Routing policies that keep apps online when capacity dips."

References / internal links:
- Benchmark draft: confluence://inference-benchmarks/draft-v2
- SLA wording: confluence://contracts/dedicated-sla-v1
- Site PR: github.com/redwood-inference/site-copy/pull/58

Conversation logs: (from Slack search)
- #gtm-copy: "Priya: prefer B for docs traffic, D for ABM — Leah: agree, but A is useful for hero tests"

---
End of doc (working draft).
